purpose: libpng is a PNG image read/write library.

functions.png_process_data_skip: `png_process_data_skip` is a deprecated/unused hook for streaming input: call it only outside `png_process_data`. In current libpng it does nothing, warns, and always returns 0, so no bytes need to be skipped.
functions.png_get_hIST: `png_get_hIST` retrieves the image’s hIST chunk data from `info_ptr`. Call it with valid `png_ptr`, `info_ptr`, and non-NULL `hist`. If `PNG_INFO_hIST` is set, it stores the histogram pointer and returns `PNG_INFO_hIST`; otherwise returns 0.
functions.png_permit_mng_features: Sets which MNG features libpng may accept. Call with a valid `png_ptr` and a bitmask; it stores only `PNG_ALL_MNG_FEATURES` bits and returns the permitted mask. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it returns 0 and changes nothing.
functions.png_set_cHRM_XYZ_fixed: Sets the cHRM chunk from fixed-point XYZ primaries. Pass `png_ptr`, `info_ptr`, and 9 XYZ values; NULL args are ignored. It stores endpoints, marks colorspace as from cHRM on success, then syncs `info_ptr` colorspace.
functions.png_set_background: `png_set_background` configures read-time compositing: it replaces alpha/tRNS transparency with a chosen background color. Use it after reading the header; `need_expand` controls palette/gray expansion, and `background_gamma_code` + gamma set how blending is done.
functions.png_get_pHYs: `png_get_pHYs` retrieves PNG physical pixel size info from `info_ptr`. Call it after reading info; pass non-NULL outputs to receive x/y pixels per unit and unit type. It returns `PNG_INFO_pHYs` only if the chunk is present and at least one requested value is written; otherwise 0.
functions.png_build_grayscale_palette: Builds a grayscale palette for indexed PNGs. Call it with bit_depth 1, 2, or 4 and a valid png_color[] buffer; it fills evenly spaced gray RGB entries. If palette is NULL, it returns. Unsupported depths aren’t handled in the shown code.
functions.png_get_chunk_malloc_max: `png_get_chunk_malloc_max()` is a simple getter for the current per-chunk allocation limit. Call it with a valid `png_ptr`; it returns `png_ptr->user_chunk_malloc_max`. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it returns `0`.
functions.png_get_eXIf: `png_get_eXIf` is a stub/compatibility API. It always warns: “does not work; use png_get_eXIf_1”, ignores `info_ptr` and `exif`, and returns `0`. Don’t use it for EXIF retrieval; call `png_get_eXIf_1` instead.
functions.png_destroy_write_struct: Destroys a write-side libpng state. Call with pointers to `png_struct*` and optional `png_info*`; it frees associated info, then the write struct, and sets `*png_ptr_ptr` to NULL. If `png_ptr_ptr` or `*png_ptr_ptr` is NULL, it does nothing.
functions.png_set_chunk_malloc_max: Sets `png_ptr->user_chunk_malloc_max`, i.e. the max malloc size allowed for a chunk. Call it on a valid `png_structrp`; if `png_ptr` is NULL, it does nothing.
functions.png_set_filter_heuristics: `png_set_filter_heuristics` is a deprecated no-op. It used to select PNG filter heuristic mode and supply weights/costs for adaptive filtering. In current libpng it ignores all args and does nothing; use `png_set_filter_heuristics_fixed` only if supported, otherwise don’t rely on it.
functions.png_set_gAMA_fixed: Sets the image file gamma in `info_ptr->colorspace`. Use it with valid `png_ptr` and `info_ptr`; if either is `NULL`, it returns immediately. It then updates colorspace gamma and syncs `info_ptr` metadata.
functions.png_get_error_ptr: `png_get_error_ptr` returns the user-supplied `error_ptr` stored in a `png_struct`. Use it to retrieve the context pointer previously set for libpng’s error/warning callbacks. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it returns `NULL`; otherwise it returns `png_ptr->error_ptr`.
functions.png_set_cHRM_XYZ: Sets PNG cHRM chromaticity via XYZ primaries. Call it with `png_ptr`/`info_ptr` and red/green/blue X,Y,Z values; it converts doubles to fixed and forwards to `png_set_cHRM_XYZ_fixed`. Invalid values are checked during conversion.
functions.png_read_row: `png_read_row` reads/decompresses one image row for the current interlace pass. Call it after `png_read_start_row`/`png_read_info`; pass `row` for output, `dsp_row` for display/transform output. If `png_ptr==NULL`, it returns.
functions.png_set_option: Sets a libpng option flag on `png_ptr`. Call with a valid `png_structrp`, an even `option` in range, and `onoff` nonzero/zero. It stores the new setting and returns the previous 2-bit value; invalid args return `PNG_OPTION_INVALID`.
functions.png_set_strip_16: `png_set_strip_16` enables the `PNG_16_TO_8` transform, telling libpng to discard the low byte of 16-bit samples and output 8-bit data. Call it before reading/processing. If transforms are already locked (`png_rtran_ok` fails), it does nothing.
functions.png_destroy_info_struct: Frees a `png_info` and its owned data. Call with a valid `png_ptr` and `info_ptr_ptr`; it NULLs `*info_ptr_ptr` first, then frees data and the struct. If `png_ptr` or `*info_ptr_ptr` is NULL, it returns doing nothing.
functions.png_get_chunk_cache_max: Returns the user-set maximum number of unknown chunks libpng will cache. Use it with a valid `png_ptr`; if `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it returns `0`. It only reports `png_ptr->user_chunk_cache_max`, no other behavior.
functions.png_malloc_default: `png_malloc_default` is libpng’s built-in allocator: it ignores any app memory hook and uses `malloc` via `png_malloc_base(NULL, size)`. Use it only with a valid `png_ptr`. If `png_ptr==NULL`, it returns `NULL`; if allocation fails, it calls `png_error(png_ptr, "Out of Memory")`.
functions.png_calloc: `png_calloc` allocates `size` bytes via `png_malloc` and zero-fills them. Use it when libpng needs cleared memory. If allocation fails, it returns `NULL`; otherwise a zeroed block.
functions.png_set_write_user_transform_fn: Sets a write-side user transform callback. Call it with a valid `png_ptr`; it marks `PNG_USER_TRANSFORM` and stores the function pointer. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it does nothing. Passing `NULL` callback just clears/sets no callback.
functions.png_set_filler: `png_set_filler` adds a filler byte/word to Gray or RGB images, mainly for read-side transforms. Use it to expand 8/16-bit Gray or 24/48-bit RGB into formats with an extra channel. On read it’s generally valid; on write it depends on the image/flags.
functions.png_set_mem_fn: `png_set_mem_fn` lets you replace libpng’s default alloc/free with your own. Call it on a valid `png_structrp` before allocations; it stores `mem_ptr`, `malloc_fn`, and `free_fn`. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it does nothing.
functions.png_get_compression_buffer_size: Returns the current compression buffer size for a `png_ptr`. Use it with a valid PNG struct; if `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it returns 0. On read structs it returns `IDAT_read_size` (or `PNG_IDAT_READ_SIZE`), otherwise the write buffer `zbuffer_size`.
functions.png_get_x_offset_microns: Returns the image x-offset in microns from an oFFs chunk. Use only when `png_ptr`/`info_ptr` are non-NULL and `PNG_INFO_oFFs` is valid; it returns `x_offset` only if `offset_unit_type==PNG_OFFSET_MICROMETER`, else 0.
functions.png_get_user_transform_ptr: Returns the `user_transform_ptr` set for libpng’s user transform callbacks. Use it to retrieve your app-specific context inside transform functions. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it returns `NULL`; otherwise it returns the stored pointer.
functions.png_convert_to_rfc1123_buffer: Formats `ptime` into an RFC1123 date string in `out[29]` (e.g. `DD Mon YYYY HH:MM:SS GMT`). Use only with valid time fields; returns 0 for NULL `out` or out-of-range year/month/day/hour/minute/second, else nonzero.
functions.png_get_IHDR: `png_get_IHDR` retrieves the image header from `info_ptr`: width, height, bit depth, color type, interlace/compression/filter methods. Pass valid `png_ptr`/`info_ptr`; any output arg may be NULL. Returns 0 if either pointer is NULL, otherwise fills requested fields.
functions.png_get_x_pixels_per_meter: Returns the X resolution in pixels/meter from a valid pHYs chunk. Use after reading info; pass non-NULL `png_ptr`/`info_ptr`. If pHYs is absent, invalid, or unit isn’t meters, it returns 0.
functions.png_get_x_offset_inches: Returns the X offset in inches from the stored micron offset. Use it after reading metadata in `info_ptr`; it just converts microns to inches in floating point. If the offset isn’t set, it follows `png_get_x_offset_microns()` behavior.
functions.png_set_longjmp_fn: `png_set_longjmp_fn` sets up libpng’s internal `jmp_buf` and the `longjmp` callback for error handling. Call it once per `png_ptr` before use. It returns the buffer pointer, or `NULL` on `png_ptr==NULL`, allocation failure, or ABI/jmp_buf size mismatch.
functions.png_set_eXIf: `png_set_eXIf` is a deprecated/disabled stub. It only issues a warning: “does not work; use png_set_eXIf_1”. It ignores `info_ptr` and `exif`, so it performs no action. Use `png_set_eXIf_1` instead.
functions.png_get_channels: Returns the image’s channel count from `info_ptr->channels`. Use it only with valid `png_ptr` and `info_ptr`; if either is NULL, it returns 0. It’s a simple query, not a setter.
functions.png_set_sPLT: `png_set_sPLT` adds one or more suggested palettes (`png_sPLT_t`) to `info_ptr` for writing. Call it with valid `png_ptr`, `info_ptr`, non-NULL `entries`, and `nentries > 0`. NULL/invalid args do nothing; allocation failure reports “too many sPLT chunks” and returns.
functions.png_get_y_offset_inches_fixed: Returns the image’s Y offset in inches as a fixed-point value. Use it with `png_ptr`/`info_ptr` after reading metadata. It converts the stored Y offset from microns to inches; if unavailable, the underlying getter determines the result.
functions.png_get_cHRM_XYZ: `png_get_cHRM_XYZ` retrieves cHRM chromaticity endpoints in XYZ form from `info_ptr` if `PNG_COLORSPACE_HAVE_ENDPOINTS` is set. Pass non-NULL output pointers as needed; NULL outputs are ignored. Returns a `png_uint_32` status, and does nothing if `png_ptr/info_ptr` are NULL or data absent.
functions.png_get_sCAL_fixed: Returns sCAL data from `info_ptr`: if `PNG_INFO_sCAL` is valid, it fills `unit`, `width`, and `height` by converting stored strings to `png_fixed_point` and returns `PNG_INFO_sCAL`. Otherwise returns 0. Requires FP support; `png_get_sCAL_s` is preferred.
functions.png_get_gAMA: `png_get_gAMA` retrieves the image’s gAMA chunk value from `info_ptr` into `*file_gamma`. Call it after reading info, with non-NULL `png_ptr`, `info_ptr`, and output ptr. Returns `PNG_INFO_gAMA` if gamma is present; otherwise 0.
functions.png_get_header_ver: `png_get_header_ver` returns the libpng header version string (`PNG_LIBPNG_VER_STRING`) used to build the library. It ignores `png_ptr`, so any valid pointer is fine. Use it to compare compile-time header version vs. runtime library version.
functions.png_set_gamma: `png_set_gamma` sets the display (screen) gamma and file gamma for gamma correction. Use it before reading the PNG header for best results; if called later, it overrides the file’s gamma info. `file_gamma` is the inverse of screen gamma.
functions.png_set_background_fixed: Sets background-composition for read transforms: blends image against `background_color`, strips alpha, and records background gamma/type. Use before reading rows. If gamma is `UNKNOWN` it warns and returns; NULL/invalid state also no-ops.
functions.png_save_uint_32: `png_save_uint_32` stores a 32-bit `png_uint_32` into a 4-byte buffer in big-endian/network order. Use it when writing PNG data fields to a byte array. It always writes 4 bytes; `buf` must be valid for 4 bytes.
functions.png_set_read_fn: Sets a custom input callback and user I/O pointer for reading PNG data. Call before reading. If `read_data_fn` is NULL, stdio builds use the default reader; otherwise the given function is used. It also clears any write callback and warns if both are set.
functions.png_get_y_offset_pixels: Returns the image’s Y offset in pixels from the oFFs chunk. Use after reading metadata, with valid `png_ptr`/`info_ptr`. It returns `y_offset` only if `PNG_INFO_oFFs` is set and unit type is `PNG_OFFSET_PIXEL`; otherwise 0.
functions.png_longjmp: `png_longjmp` is libpng’s wrapper for `longjmp`. Use it instead of calling `longjmp(png_ptr->jmpbuf, val)` directly. If `longjmp_fn` and `jmp_buf_ptr` are set, it jumps there; otherwise it aborts the process. It must not return.
functions.png_get_compression_type: `png_get_compression_type` returns `info_ptr->compression_type` for a valid `png_ptr`/`info_ptr`. Use it after reading/setting info. If either pointer is `NULL`, it returns `0`.
functions.png_access_version_number: `png_access_version_number()` returns libpng’s build-time version as a `png_uint_32` (`PNG_LIBPNG_VER`). Use it to query the library version at runtime; it takes no args and has no special cases—just returns the compiled-in version number.
functions.png_get_x_offset_inches_fixed: Returns the X offset in inches as a `png_fixed_point`. It just converts `png_get_x_offset_microns()` via `png_fixed_inches_from_microns()`. Use it with valid `png_ptr`/`info_ptr`; if the micron offset is unavailable, behavior follows that getter.
functions.png_image_begin_read_from_file: Opens `file_name` in binary read mode, initializes a `png_image` for reading, and reads the PNG header. Use only with a valid `image` (`version==PNG_IMAGE_VERSION`) and non-NULL filename. On success it owns the FILE*; on failure it reports an error and closes any opened file.
functions.png_write_end: `png_write_end` finishes PNG writing. Call it after all IDAT/image data are written; `info_ptr` may supply trailing chunks (e.g. tIME/text). If no IDATs were written, it errors. If `png_ptr` is NULL, it returns.
functions.png_handle_as_unknown: `png_handle_as_unknown` checks `chunk_name` against libpng’s chunk list and returns that chunk’s stored “keep” policy. Use it to decide whether a chunk needs special unknown-chunk handling. NULL/empty list or no match => default handling.
functions.png_get_rowbytes: `png_get_rowbytes` returns `info_ptr->rowbytes`: the byte count needed for one transformed image row. Call it with valid `png_ptr` and `info_ptr`; if either is `NULL`, it returns `0`.
functions.png_get_cHRM_XYZ_fixed: Returns cHRM chromaticity endpoints in fixed-point XYZ. Use after `png_read_info`/when `info_ptr` has `PNG_COLORSPACE_HAVE_ENDPOINTS`; pass NULL for outputs you don’t need. If `png_ptr`/`info_ptr` are NULL or no endpoints exist, it returns 0 and writes nothing.
functions.png_get_PLTE: Retrieves the image’s PLTE palette from `info_ptr`. Use only after reading info; pass non-NULL `png_ptr`, `info_ptr`, `palette`, and `num_palette`. If `PNG_INFO_PLTE` is set, it fills both and returns `PNG_INFO_PLTE`; otherwise returns 0.
functions.png_write_chunk: `png_write_chunk` is a thin wrapper to write one PNG chunk: it converts the 4-byte chunk name and calls `png_write_complete_chunk` to emit size, type, optional data, and CRC. Use it with a valid `png_structrp`, chunk name, data pointer, and length.
functions.png_get_gAMA_fixed: `png_get_gAMA_fixed` retrieves the image’s stored gAMA value as a fixed-point gamma. Call it with valid `png_ptr`, `info_ptr`, and output pointer. It returns `PNG_INFO_gAMA` and fills `*file_gamma` only if gamma is present; otherwise returns 0.
functions.png_write_info_before_PLTE: Writes the PNG signature and IHDR before PLTE. Call it once with valid `png_ptr`/`info_ptr`; if either is NULL it returns. Repeated calls are ignored via `PNG_WROTE_INFO_BEFORE_PLTE`.
functions.png_set_expand_gray_1_2_4_to_8: Enables expansion of low-bit-depth grayscale (1/2/4-bit) to 8-bit during read. Call it on a valid `png_structrp` before row reading; it just sets `PNG_EXPAND` if transforms are allowed, otherwise it returns with no effect.
functions.png_set_text_compression_mem_level: Sets the zlib memory level used when compressing text chunks. Call it with a valid `png_structrp` before writing text; `NULL` does nothing. It simply stores `mem_level` in `png_ptr->zlib_text_mem_level` with no validation.
functions.png_get_pHYs_dpi: Returns pHYs metadata in DPI form. Call after reading info, with non-NULL png_ptr/info_ptr and a valid pHYs chunk. It fills requested outputs (x/y/unit) if pointers are non-NULL and returns PNG_INFO_pHYs when data was provided, else 0.
functions.png_set_sig_bytes: `png_set_sig_bytes` tells libpng how many PNG signature bytes you already consumed before calling `png_read_info`. Use it after pre-reading 0–8 magic bytes. `num_bytes<0` is treated as 0; `>8` triggers `png_error`; `NULL` `png_ptr` is ignored.
functions.png_set_alpha_mode_fixed: Sets alpha handling + gamma for output. Call before reading transforms. `output_gamma` is screen decode gamma; must be ~1..100. Invalid range errors. If supported, it may premultiply/compose alpha and uses file gamma as reciprocal of output gamma.
functions.png_chunk_benign_error: `png_chunk_benign_error` reports a chunk-related error that may be treated as warning or fatal. Use it during chunk read handling. If `PNG_FLAG_BENIGN_ERRORS_WARN` is set, it calls `png_chunk_warning`; otherwise `png_chunk_error`.
functions.png_set_text_compression_method: Sets the zlib compression method for PNG text chunks. Call it with a valid `png_structrp`; if `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it returns. Any `method` other than 8 triggers a warning, but the value is still stored.
functions.png_set_sCAL_fixed:
`png_set_sCAL_fixed` stores the sCAL chunk using fixed-point width/height. It requires both >0; otherwise it warns and ignores the value. On success it converts them to ASCII and calls `png_set_sCAL_s`. Use it to set pixel size metadata in `info_ptr`.
Do not call png_set_sCAL_fixed multiple times on the same png_info object without clearing or recreating that metadata container. Set sCAL at most once per png_info, or destroy the current png_struct/png_info and create fresh ones before setting a new sCAL value.
functions.png_get_y_pixels_per_inch: Returns the image’s Y resolution in pixels/inch, converting from the stored pixels/meter value. Use it with a valid `png_ptr` and `info_ptr`. If no Y ppi is set, it reflects the underlying meter value conversion (likely 0).
functions.png_set_invalid: `png_set_invalid` clears selected bits in `info_ptr->valid`. Use it after your app frees chunk data so libpng knows that info is no longer valid. It does nothing if `png_ptr` or `info_ptr` is `NULL`; it only updates the validity mask.
functions.png_get_cHRM: `png_get_cHRM` retrieves chromaticity endpoints from `info_ptr` if available, even when they came from iCCP/sRGB, not just a cHRM chunk. Pass non-NULL output pointers as needed; returns endpoints only when `PNG_COLORSPACE_HAVE_ENDPOINTS` is set, else nothing.
functions.png_progressive_combine_row: Used with progressive read callbacks to update `old_row` from libpng’s internal row buffer. `new_row` is only a non-NULL flag; its value is ignored. If `png_ptr` is NULL, it does nothing. If `new_row` is NULL, no combine occurs.
functions.png_set_tRNS: `png_set_tRNS` stores tRNS transparency info in `info_ptr` for later PNG writing/reading. Call it with valid `png_ptr`/`info_ptr`; pass either palette alpha bytes (`trans_alpha`, `num_trans`) or a transparent color (`trans_color`). NULL pointers return immediately; invalid/too-large counts are ignored.
functions.png_set_filter_heuristics_fixed: A no-op stub for setting PNG filter heuristic weights/costs. Intended for write-time filter selection tuning, but this build ignores all args and has no effect. Use only if your libpng was built with weighted-filter support.
functions.png_get_current_pass_number: Returns the current interlace pass index from `png_ptr->pass`. Use it only with a valid `png_ptr`; if `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it returns `8` as an invalid sentinel.
functions.png_get_pixels_per_inch: Returns the image resolution in pixels/inch, derived from the stored pixels/meter value. Call it with valid `png_ptr` and `info_ptr` after reading metadata. If no pHYs/resolution is present, it returns 0.
functions.png_set_scale_16: `png_set_scale_16` requests libpng to accurately scale 16-bit samples down to 8-bit during read. Call it on a valid `png_ptr` before reading rows. If read transforms aren’t allowed (`png_rtran_ok` fails), it does nothing; otherwise it sets `PNG_SCALE_16_TO_8`.
functions.png_save_int_32: `png_save_int_32` stores a signed 32-bit integer into a 4-byte PNG buffer. Use it when writing an `png_int_32` value to bytes; it just casts to `png_uint_32` and calls `png_save_uint_32`, so the raw 32-bit bit pattern is saved.
functions.png_convert_from_time_t: Converts a `time_t` to `png_time` using `gmtime()` then `png_convert_from_struct_tm()`. Use it to fill a `png_time` from a Unix timestamp. If `gmtime()` fails/returns null, behavior depends on `png_convert_from_struct_tm()` handling.
functions.png_set_oFFs: Sets the PNG oFFs chunk: stores image x/y offsets and unit type in `info_ptr`, marking `PNG_INFO_oFFs` valid. Call with non-NULL `png_ptr`/`info_ptr`; if either is NULL, it returns with no effect.
functions.png_get_user_width_max: Returns the user-set maximum image width from `png_ptr`. Use it to query the limit previously configured in the PNG read/write struct. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it returns `0`.
functions.png_get_sCAL_s: `png_get_sCAL_s` reads the sCAL chunk from `info_ptr`. Use it after `png_read_info`; it fills `unit`, `width`, and `height` with the stored strings. Returns `PNG_INFO_sCAL` if present, else 0. It does not allocate or copy data.
functions.png_get_sCAL: `png_get_sCAL` retrieves the sCAL chunk from `info_ptr`: it returns `PNG_INFO_sCAL` if present, fills `unit`, `width`, and `height` by converting stored strings to `double`, else returns 0. Use only when floating-point support is available.
functions.png_image_finish_read: `png_image_finish_read` completes a png_image read into `buffer`, using `background`/`colormap` if needed. It validates `image` version and checks `row_stride` for signed-32-bit overflow; `row_stride==0` means use the natural row size. Returns failure on invalid args/overflow.
functions.png_get_bKGD: `png_get_bKGD` retrieves the image’s stored bKGD chunk. Call it with valid `png_ptr`, `info_ptr`, and a non-NULL `background` pointer. If `PNG_INFO_bKGD` is set, it returns that flag and gives you `info_ptr->background`; otherwise it returns 0.
functions.png_set_swap: `png_set_swap` enables byte-swapping for 16-bit PNG data. Call it on a valid `png_ptr`; if `bit_depth == 16`, it sets `PNG_SWAP_BYTES`. If `png_ptr` is NULL or depth isn’t 16, it does nothing.
functions.png_set_text: `png_set_text` stores `num_text` text entries into `info_ptr` via `png_set_text_2`. Use it after valid `png_ptr`/`info_ptr` are set. If memory allocation fails, it raises `png_error("Insufficient memory to store text")`.
functions.png_set_bgr: `png_set_bgr` enables the `PNG_BGR` transform, telling libpng to treat pixel bytes as BGR instead of RGB. Call it on a valid `png_structrp` before reading/writing image data. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it does nothing.
functions.png_get_sRGB: `png_get_sRGB` retrieves the PNG sRGB chunk info. Use it with valid `png_ptr`/`info_ptr`; if `PNG_INFO_sRGB` is present and `file_srgb_intent` is non-NULL, it stores the rendering intent and returns `PNG_INFO_sRGB`. Otherwise it returns 0.
functions.png_init_io: `png_init_io` sets `png_ptr->io_ptr` to a `FILE*`, initializing libpng’s I/O to use the default stdio-based functions. Call it once before read/write ops. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it returns immediately; otherwise it just stores `fp`.
functions.png_set_text_compression_level: Sets the zlib compression level for non-IDAT text chunks. Call it with a valid `png_ptr` before writing text; if `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it returns. It only stores `level` in `png_ptr->zlib_text_level`.
functions.png_write_flush: `png_write_flush` forces a sync flush of the current PNG output stream. Call it with a valid `png_ptr` during writing; if `png_ptr` is `NULL` or all rows are already written, it returns immediately. It flushes pending IDAT data and resets `flush_rows`.
functions.png_set_compression_level: Sets libpng’s zlib compression level for later write/compression operations. Call it with a valid `png_structrp`; if `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it does nothing. It simply stores `level` in `png_ptr->zlib_level` and does no validation.
functions.png_set_compression_strategy: Sets libpng’s zlib compression strategy. Call it with a valid `png_ptr`; if `png_ptr==NULL` it does nothing. It marks the strategy as custom (`PNG_FLAG_ZLIB_CUSTOM_STRATEGY`) and stores the given `strategy` in `png_ptr->zlib_strategy`, overriding libpng’s dynamic selection.
functions.png_data_freer: `png_data_freer` sets per-`png_info` ownership flags for selected data (`mask`): `PNG_DESTROY_WILL_FREE_DATA` marks libpng to free it, `PNG_USER_WILL_FREE_DATA` clears that. It only affects the given `info_ptr`; NULL args return, unknown `freer` triggers `png_error`.
functions.png_set_rows: Sets `info_ptr->row_pointers` for `png_write_png()`. Call with valid `png_ptr`/`info_ptr` and an array of scanline pointers. If either is `NULL`, it returns. Replacing existing rows frees old ones; non-`NULL` rows mark `PNG_INFO_IDAT` valid.
functions.png_get_pixels_per_meter: Returns square image resolution from `pHYs` data in pixels/meter. Call with non-NULL `png_ptr` and `info_ptr`; it returns `x_pixels_per_unit` only if `PNG_INFO_pHYs` is valid, unit is meters, and X==Y. Otherwise returns `0`.
functions.png_set_sCAL_s:
`png_set_sCAL_s` stores the sCAL chunk in `info_ptr` using string width/height. Use it with `unit` 1 or 2 and valid nonempty positive numeric strings. NULL `png_ptr/info_ptr` returns; invalid unit/strings trigger `png_error`.
Treat png_set_sCAL_s as a one-time setter for a given png_info instance. Pass valid positive width/height strings and avoid repeated updates on the same info_ptr because previous internal string allocations may be replaced and leaked.
functions.png_set_rgb_to_gray: Sets RGB→gray conversion coefficients. Use `png_set_rgb_to_gray[_fixed]` before reading/conversion. It forwards to the fixed version. `error_action` controls behavior if coefficients are invalid; `png_get_rgb_to_gray_status` reports whether conversion was used.
functions.png_error:
`png_error` reports a **fatal libpng error** and does **not return**. Use it when PNG processing cannot continue; it may strip `#nnnn` prefixes/text based on `png_ptr` flags, then invokes libpng’s error handling/jump mechanism.
Do not use an error callback that unconditionally aborts for normal libpng validation failures. Libpng expects errors to be handled via its setjmp/longjmp mechanism: establish setjmp(png_jmpbuf(png_ptr)) before libpng calls and make the custom error handler longjmp back (or use the default behavior), so invalid input is reported and recovered from instead of terminating the process.
functions.png_create_write_struct_2: `png_create_write_struct_2` creates a libpng write struct with user-supplied error/warning handlers and custom memory alloc/free functions. Use it before writing PNGs; on version mismatch or init failure it returns `NULL`. Defaults zlib write settings if creation succeeds.
functions.png_image_free: `png_image_free` releases resources owned by a `png_image`. Call it when done with an image. It only frees if `image`, `image->opaque` are non-NULL and not in an error-handling context (`error_buf == NULL`); otherwise it does nothing, deferring cleanup.
functions.png_set_compression_window_bits: Sets zlib PNG compression window size for writes. Use with `png_ptr`; values are clamped to 8..15 (256B..32KB) with warnings. `NULL` does nothing. It prevents non-standard raw deflate/gzip PNG output.
functions.png_get_bit_depth: `png_get_bit_depth` returns the image bit depth from `info_ptr`. Call it with valid `png_ptr` and `info_ptr`; if either is `NULL`, it returns `0`. It does no other processing.
functions.png_set_tRNS_to_alpha: `png_set_tRNS_to_alpha` enables expansion of a PNG tRNS chunk into an alpha channel. Call it on a valid `png_ptr` before reading rows. If `png_rtran_ok` fails, it does nothing; otherwise it sets `PNG_EXPAND | PNG_EXPAND_tRNS` in the transform flags.
functions.png_get_filter_type: Returns the filter type stored in `info_ptr`. Call it with valid `png_ptr` and `info_ptr`; if either is `NULL`, it returns `0`. It’s a simple getter, not a setter or validator.
functions.png_set_swap_alpha: `png_set_swap_alpha` enables the `PNG_SWAP_ALPHA` transform on `png_ptr`. Call it before reading/writing image data to swap the alpha channel with the adjacent color component. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it does nothing.
functions.png_image_write_to_memory: Writes an image into a caller buffer, or just counts required bytes if `memory==NULL`. Use only with a valid `png_image` version, `memory_bytes` and `buffer` non-NULL. If init fails or args are invalid, it returns failure; NULL-memory case sets `*memory_bytes=0`.
functions.png_get_mem_ptr: `png_get_mem_ptr` returns the user-supplied `mem_ptr` stored in a `png_struct`. Use it to retrieve the pointer associated with custom memory alloc/free callbacks. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it returns `NULL`; otherwise it returns `png_ptr->mem_ptr`.
functions.png_warning: `png_warning` reports a non-fatal libpng warning. Call it with a valid `png_ptr` and message; if `warning_fn` is set, it uses that callback, otherwise the default handler. It may strip leading `#... ` error numbers/text before reporting.
functions.png_sig_cmp: `png_sig_cmp` checks whether bytes in `sig` match the PNG 8-byte signature. Use it to validate a file header; it returns 0 on match, nonzero on mismatch. `num_to_check==0` or `start>7` fails, and it only compares the requested range.
functions.png_set_IHDR: `png_set_IHDR` stores the PNG IHDR fields in `info_ptr` for writing: width/height, bit depth, color type, interlace, compression, filter. Call it after creating `png_ptr/info_ptr`; NULL pointers are ignored. It validates via `png_check_IHDR` and sets channel count from color type.
functions.png_set_iCCP: `png_set_iCCP` stores an ICC profile in `info_ptr` for PNG write info. Use it with valid `png_ptr/info_ptr/name/profile`; `compression_type` must be `PNG_COMPRESSION_TYPE_BASE` or it errors. It validates/syncs colorspace first and skips copying if the profile is bad/inconsistent.
functions.png_image_write_to_stdio:
Writes a `png_image` to a `FILE*`. Use only with valid `image` version, non-NULL `file`/`buffer`; it initializes write state, sets stdio I/O, then writes via `png_safe_execute` and frees the image. Returns success/failure.
Yes, this crash is caused by misuse of the API. When calling png_image_write_to_stdio, ensure the input buffer size and row_stride match libpng's expected layout for image.format. In particular, compute bytes per pixel using bytes, not bits: use PNG_IMAGE_SAMPLE_CHANNELS(format) * (PNG_IMAGE_SAMPLE_SIZE(format) / 8), and for linear formats account for 16-bit samples correctly. Allocate at least abs(row_stride) * height bytes when row_stride != 0, or PNG_IMAGE_SIZE(image) bytes when row_stride == 0. Pass row_stride as the number of bytes between rows, and if negative, ensure the buffer starts at the last row as required by the API. Also provide a valid colormap when using colormapped formats, and keep buffer memory alive for the duration of the call.
functions.png_get_pixel_aspect_ratio: Returns the pixel aspect ratio from `pHYs` data as `y_pixels_per_unit / x_pixels_per_unit`. Use only after reading `info_ptr`; if `png_ptr/info_ptr` is NULL, `pHYs` absent, or `x_pixels_per_unit==0`, it returns `0.0`.
functions.png_get_y_pixels_per_meter: Returns the image’s Y resolution in pixels/meter from a valid `pHYs` chunk. Call with non-NULL `png_ptr` and `info_ptr`; if `pHYs` is absent, invalid, or unit isn’t meters, it returns 0.
functions.png_set_invert_alpha: `png_set_invert_alpha()` enables the `PNG_INVERT_ALPHA` transform on a valid `png_ptr`. Use it before reading rows to invert alpha values during decoding. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it does nothing.
functions.png_get_rgb_to_gray_status: Returns the current RGB→gray conversion status stored in `png_ptr`. Use it after libpng grayscale conversion processing to query the result. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it returns `0`.
functions.png_get_cHRM_fixed: `png_get_cHRM_fixed` retrieves cHRM chromaticity endpoints from `info_ptr` into fixed-point outputs. Pass valid `png_ptr`/`info_ptr`; any output arg may be NULL. It returns `PNG_INFO_cHRM` only if endpoints exist, otherwise 0.
functions.png_get_io_ptr: `png_get_io_ptr` returns the user-supplied I/O pointer stored in `png_ptr->io_ptr`. Use it after setting custom read/write callbacks to retrieve your context. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it returns `NULL`.
functions.png_set_cHRM_fixed: Sets PNG cHRM chromaticity metadata from fixed-point white/red/green/blue xy values. Call with valid `png_ptr`/`info_ptr`; NULL returns immediately. If values are accepted, it marks colorspace as from cHRM and syncs `info_ptr`; otherwise no update.
functions.png_set_gamma_fixed: Sets libpng’s gamma correction for reading. Use with positive fixed-point screen_gamma and file_gamma before row processing. Negative reserved flags are translated; 0/negative now errors. If transform setup isn’t allowed, it returns without effect.
functions.png_set_invert_mono: `png_set_invert_mono` enables the `PNG_INVERT_MONO` transform on a valid `png_ptr`. Use it before reading/converting image data to flip monochrome bit meaning. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it does nothing.
functions.png_set_user_transform_info: Sets user-transform context for libpng read callbacks: stores `user_transform_ptr`, bit depth, and channel count. Call before `png_start_read_image`/`png_read_update_info`; if called after on a read struct, it errors and returns. Null `png_ptr` is ignored.
functions.png_get_libpng_ver: `png_get_libpng_ver(png_ptr)` returns the libpng version string used to build the library. Use it to query version info from a valid `png_ptr`. It simply forwards to `png_get_header_ver(png_ptr)` and returns that string.
functions.png_get_pCAL: `png_get_pCAL` retrieves a PNG pCAL chunk from `info_ptr`. Use it only after reading info, and pass non-NULL output pointers. If `PNG_INFO_pCAL` is set, it fills purpose/X0/X1/type/nparams/units/params and returns `PNG_INFO_pCAL`; otherwise returns 0.
functions.png_set_add_alpha: Adds an alpha/filler byte to gray/RGB images via `png_set_filler`. Use it on a valid `png_ptr` before read transforms. If `PNG_FILLER` is set, it also marks `PNG_ADD_ALPHA`; if `png_ptr` is NULL, it returns immediately.
functions.png_get_x_offset_pixels: Returns the x offset from the oFFs chunk, but only if `png_ptr`/`info_ptr` are non-NULL, `PNG_INFO_oFFs` is valid, and the unit is pixels. Otherwise it returns 0. Use it after reading metadata.
functions.png_set_unknown_chunks: Sets `info_ptr`’s list of unknown PNG chunks for read/write handling. Call with valid `png_ptr`, `info_ptr`, non-NULL `unknowns`, and `num_unknowns>0`. If unknown-chunk support is disabled for the current mode, it reports an app error and returns.
functions.png_destroy_read_struct: Destroys a read-side PNG context and frees associated `png_info` structs. Call with pointers to `png_struct`, `info`, and optional `end_info`; any NULL arg is ignored. If `png_ptr` is NULL, it returns. On success, it NULLs `*png_ptr_ptr` and frees the read state.
functions.png_read_rows: `png_read_rows` is a convenience wrapper to read multiple image rows at once. Pass arrays of row buffers; if `display_row` is non-NULL, each row is also sent there. If `png_ptr` is NULL, it returns; if `row` is NULL, nothing is read.
functions.png_set_interlace_handling: Enables libpng to handle interlaced PNGs during reading. Call it before `png_read_update_info` or `png_start_read_image`. It sets the interlace transform and returns 7 for interlaced images, otherwise 1. You still read each row for every pass.
functions.png_write_png: `png_write_png` is a high-level write helper: it writes PNG header/info, applies requested write transforms, then writes image data. Use it only with valid `png_ptr`/`info_ptr` and existing rows (`PNG_INFO_IDAT`); otherwise it returns or errors. Unsupported transforms trigger an app error.
functions.png_write_rows: `png_write_rows` is a convenience wrapper to write multiple image rows in order. Pass a `png_structrp`, a row-pointer array, and `num_rows`; it calls `png_write_row` for each `*rp`. If `png_ptr==NULL`, it returns immediately.
functions.png_get_io_chunk_type: Returns the 4-byte PNG chunk type currently being processed by libpng (`png_ptr->chunk_name`). Use it during I/O callbacks/error handling to inspect the active chunk. If no chunk is active, it returns whatever `chunk_name` currently holds.
functions.png_set_rgb_to_gray_fixed: Enables RGB→gray transform with fixed-point red/green weights. Call before reading rows, after IHDR is known. `error_action` selects none/warn/error on non-grayable input; palette images are checked and may trigger an error.
functions.png_create_info_struct: `png_create_info_struct` allocates and zero-initializes a `png_info` object for a valid `png_struct`. Call it after `png_create_read_struct`/`write_struct`; it returns `NULL` if `png_ptr` is `NULL` or allocation fails. It avoids triggering libpng errors.
functions.png_set_cHRM: `png_set_cHRM` sets the PNG cHRM chunk (white point + RGB primaries) in `info_ptr`. Use it before writing the image; it converts doubles to fixed-point and delegates to `png_set_cHRM_fixed`. It doesn’t compute values or read data.
functions.png_get_y_offset_microns: Returns the stored image Y offset in micrometers from `info_ptr` when `PNG_INFO_oFFs` is valid and `offset_unit_type==PNG_OFFSET_MICROMETER`. Use after reading metadata. If unsupported, args null, invalid, or other units, it returns 0.
functions.png_get_sPLT: Returns the number of sPLT palettes in `info_ptr` and sets `*spalettes` to the internal palette list. Use with valid `png_ptr`, `info_ptr`, and output pointer. If any arg is NULL, it returns 0 and does nothing.
functions.png_set_progressive_read_fn: Sets callbacks for libpng’s progressive/push reader. Call it after `png_create_read_struct`; pass user data plus `info_fn`, `row_fn`, `end_fn`. If `png_ptr` is NULL, it returns. It stores the callbacks and installs push buffering via `png_set_read_fn`.
functions.png_write_row: `png_write_row` writes one image row to a PNG stream. Call it after `png_write_info`; on the first row it checks setup/transforms. If `png_ptr` is NULL it returns. Missing `png_write_info` triggers `png_error`; unsupported set transforms may warn.
functions.png_set_pHYs: `png_set_pHYs` stores pHYs metadata in `info_ptr`: X/Y pixels per unit and unit type. Call it with valid `png_ptr`/`info_ptr`; if either is NULL it returns. It just sets fields and marks `PNG_INFO_pHYs` valid.
functions.png_create_read_struct_2: Creates a libpng read struct with custom error/warn handlers and custom alloc/free hooks. Use it before reading PNG data. On success it marks the struct as read-mode, sets read defaults, and may enable benign/app warning behavior; on failure it returns NULL.
functions.png_read_end: `png_read_end` finishes PNG input after image rows: it flushes any pending IDAT/zlib state, then reads remaining chunks to the end. Call it after `png_read_image`/row reads. If `png_ptr==NULL`, it returns; palette index issues may be reported as benign errors.
functions.png_set_expand_16: `png_set_expand_16()` enables read-side expansion to 16-bit channels. Use it before `png_read_info()`/row reads. It sets `PNG_EXPAND_16|PNG_EXPAND|PNG_EXPAND_tRNS`, so palette data becomes RGB and any tRNS chunk is expanded; if transforms aren’t allowed, it does nothing.
functions.png_get_user_chunk_ptr: Returns the `user_chunk_ptr` stored in `png_ptr`. Use it to retrieve the application-defined pointer for custom chunk handling. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it returns `NULL`.
functions.png_chunk_warning: `png_chunk_warning` reports a non-fatal libpng warning, prefixing the current chunk name to the message. Call it with `png_ptr` and a warning string. If `png_ptr` is NULL, it passes the message to `png_warning`; otherwise it formats then warns.
functions.png_info_init_3: `png_info_init_3` is a deprecated helper to initialize/reinitialize a `png_info` struct, using default allocation. If the passed buffer is too small, it frees it and allocates a new one; otherwise it zeroes the struct. Use newer libpng init APIs instead.
functions.png_benign_error: `png_benign_error` reports a non-fatal libpng problem. If `PNG_FLAG_BENIGN_ERRORS_WARN` is set, it warns; otherwise it treats it as an error. In read mode with a current chunk, it uses chunk-specific warn/error; else normal warn/error.
functions.png_set_write_fn: `png_set_write_fn` installs custom write/flush callbacks and user I/O state for PNG output. Use it before writing; `io_ptr` is passed to callbacks. If `write_data_fn` is NULL, libpng uses its default write; flush may be NULL when unsupported/unused. If `png_ptr` is NULL, it returns immediately.
functions.png_set_shift: `png_set_shift` enables the PNG_SHIFT transform and stores the “true” bit depths in `png_ptr->shift`. Use it before reading/conversion to expand low-bit-depth samples to legal depths. If `png_ptr` is NULL, it does nothing.
functions.png_create_write_struct: Creates and initializes a `png_struct` for PNG writing. Use it first, passing libpng version and optional error/warn callbacks. If user memory support is off, it uses default allocation; otherwise it delegates to `png_create_write_struct_2`.
functions.png_write_info: `png_write_info` starts PNG output: it writes the IHDR-related info and any required chunks (e.g. PLTE, tRNS, text) from `info_ptr`. Call it after setting up `png_ptr/info_ptr`, before writing image rows. NULL args return; missing PLTE for palette images is an error.
functions.png_get_x_pixels_per_inch: Returns the image X resolution in pixels/inch, derived from the stored X pixels/meter value. Use it after reading metadata via `png_ptr`/`info_ptr`. If no X pHYs data is present, it returns the converted value from that field’s default/zero state.
functions.png_get_unknown_chunks: Returns the count of unknown chunks in `info_ptr` and sets `*unknowns` to the chunk array. Use only with non-NULL `png_ptr`, `info_ptr`, and output pointer. If any arg is NULL, it returns 0 and leaves nothing set.
functions.png_set_error_fn: Sets libpng’s per-`png_struct` error/warning callbacks and user error context. Call it after creating `png_ptr`. If `png_ptr==NULL`, it does nothing. Stores `error_ptr`; `warning_fn` is saved only when warnings are enabled.
functions.png_set_quantize: `png_set_quantize` enables PNG quantization (`PNG_QUANTIZE`) to reduce a palette to `maximum_colors`. If `full_quantize==0`, it builds a direct index map; otherwise it uses full quantization. If `num_palette>maximum_colors` and `histogram` is given, least-used colors are discarded.
functions.png_set_PLTE:
`png_set_PLTE` stores a PLTE palette in `info_ptr` for indexed-color PNGs. Use it with a valid `png_ptr/info_ptr`, a palette array, and count. For palette images, count must be ≤ `1<<bit_depth`; otherwise ≤ `PNG_MAX_PALETTE_LENGTH`. Invalid length errors on palette images, warns/returns on others.
Call this only with a valid palette configuration. For indexed-color PNGs (PNG_COLOR_TYPE_PALETTE), ensure the palette pointer is non-null and num_palette is in the legal range 1..(1<<bit_depth) and never exceeds PNG_MAX_PALETTE_LENGTH. For non-palette color types, either avoid calling png_set_PLTE unless a suggested palette is intentionally provided, or ensure any provided palette length is valid per libpng rules. Do not pass num_palette==0 with a non-null/meaningless palette and expect success.
functions.png_get_user_height_max: Returns the current per-image height limit set in `png_ptr->user_height_max`. Use it to query the user-defined maximum height. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it returns `0`.
functions.png_set_read_status_fn: Sets a callback for read progress. Call it with a valid `png_structrp`; passing `NULL` does nothing. The function simply stores `read_row_fn` in `png_ptr`, so later row-reading code can invoke it.
functions.png_get_header_version: Returns a compile-time header version string, not tied to `png_ptr` (it’s unused). Use it to query the libpng header version/date. If `__STDC__` is defined, it appends newline and, when read support is off, “(NO READ SUPPORT)”.
functions.png_save_uint_16: `png_save_uint_16` stores a 16-bit unsigned value into a 2-byte buffer in big-endian/network order. Use it when writing PNG data fields. It always writes `buf[0]` = high byte, `buf[1]` = low byte; caller must provide at least 2 bytes.
functions.png_set_compression_method: Sets the PNG zlib compression method in `png_ptr`. Use it on a valid `png_structrp`; if `png_ptr` is NULL, it returns. Any `method` other than 8 triggers a warning, but the value is still stored. PNG supports only method 8.
functions.png_get_pixel_aspect_ratio_fixed: Returns the pixel aspect ratio as a fixed-point value from pHYs: `y_pixels_per_unit / x_pixels_per_unit`. Use only when `png_ptr/info_ptr` are valid and pHYs exists; otherwise it returns 0.
functions.png_get_y_offset_inches: Returns the image’s Y offset in inches, derived from the stored micron offset. Use it with valid `png_ptr`/`info_ptr`; it just converts the micron value to float. If no offset is present, it follows `png_get_y_offset_microns`’s result.
functions.png_set_flush: `png_set_flush` sets the row interval for output flushes during PNG writing. Use it on a valid `png_ptr`; pass `nrows >= 0`. `0` disables flushing. Negative values are treated as `0`. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it does nothing.
functions.png_get_uint_32: `png_get_uint_32` converts 4 bytes in `buf` from PNG/network byte order (big-endian) into a `png_uint_32`. Use it when reading 32-bit values from PNG data. It just combines the 4 bytes; no validation or bounds checking.
functions.png_free_data: `png_free_data` frees libpng-owned fields in `png_info` per `mask` (e.g. text). Use it only with valid `png_ptr`/`info_ptr`; `num==-1` frees all items, otherwise only item `num`. If the requested data isn’t present or not marked in `free_me`, it does nothing.
functions.png_write_sig: Writes the PNG 8-byte file signature to the output stream. Use it at the start of PNG writing; `sig_bytes` lets it write only the remaining bytes if some were already sent. If `sig_bytes < 3`, it marks the signature as present.
functions.png_get_eXIf_1: Retrieves the stored eXIf chunk data from `info_ptr`. Use with valid `png_ptr`/`info_ptr` and non-NULL `exif`; on success it fills `num_exif` and `*exif` and returns `PNG_INFO_eXIf`. Otherwise returns 0.
functions.png_start_read_image: Starts row/image read setup. Call once before reading image data, typically after `png_read_update_info`. If row init hasn’t run, it calls `png_read_start_row`; if called twice, it reports a duplicate-call app error.
functions.png_chunk_error: `png_chunk_error` is a noreturn helper for reporting a chunk-specific fatal error. Call it with `png_ptr` and an error string; it prepends the current chunk name via `png_format_buffer()` then invokes `png_error()`. If `png_ptr==NULL`, it just calls `png_error()` with the original message.
functions.png_process_data_pause: Used only inside `png_process_data` to pause parsing. `save!=0` saves pending bytes and returns 0. Otherwise it returns remaining unsaved bytes to resend; if all data is cached/saved, it returns 0.
functions.png_get_color_type: Returns the PNG image’s color_type from `info_ptr`. Use it after checking both `png_ptr` and `info_ptr` are valid; otherwise it returns 0. It simply exposes the stored color type, with no extra processing.
functions.png_set_alpha_mode: Design: set libpng alpha handling for output gamma/colorspace, optionally premultiplying alpha. Use after read setup with a mode like PNG_ALPHA_PNG. Behavior: it just converts `output_gamma` then calls `png_set_alpha_mode_fixed`; no extra logic here.
functions.png_set_sCAL: `png_set_sCAL` stores the PNG sCAL physical scale as ASCII. Use it only with `width>0` and `height>0`; otherwise it warns and ignores the value. It converts doubles to strings, then calls `png_set_sCAL_s` to save `unit`, width, and height.
functions.png_set_crc_action: `png_set_crc_action` sets how libpng handles CRC errors in critical and ancillary chunks. Call it on a valid `png_ptr` before reading. Critical chunks can be kept or cause error; discarding critical data is invalid and warns.
functions.png_get_signature: `png_get_signature` returns `info_ptr->signature` if both `png_ptr` and `info_ptr` are non-NULL; otherwise it returns `NULL`. Use it only after you have valid PNG and info structs to read the header signature bytes.
functions.png_write_chunk_start: `png_write_chunk_start` begins writing a PNG chunk by emitting its length and 4-byte name. Use it with a valid `png_structrp`, chunk name string, and data length before writing the chunk data/end. It just forwards to `png_write_chunk_header`.
functions.png_malloc_warn:
`png_malloc_warn` allocates `size` bytes via libpng’s allocator. Use it with a valid `png_ptr`. If allocation fails, it returns `NULL` and emits `png_warning(png_ptr, "Out of memory")`; if `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it just returns `NULL` without warning.
Do not invoke png_malloc_warn directly for this workflow; it is an internal allocation helper used by libpng. Prevent the leak by using the higher-level sCAL setters correctly rather than relying on internal allocation behavior.
functions.png_read_update_info: Updates `info_ptr`/row state after setting read transforms, before reading rows. Call once after `png_read_info` and before `png_read_row`/`png_read_image`. If called twice, it reports a duplicate-call error; if `png_ptr` is NULL, it does nothing.
functions.png_set_pCAL: `png_set_pCAL` stores a pCAL chunk in `info_ptr` for writing: calibration purpose, X0/X1, equation type, params, and units. It validates pointers and type (0–3); invalid args report write error/return. Use only with non-NULL required inputs.
functions.png_free_default: `png_free_default` is libpng’s default deallocator. Use it to free memory previously allocated by libpng’s default allocator. If `png_ptr` or `ptr` is `NULL`, it returns immediately; otherwise it calls `free(ptr)`. Deprecated.
functions.png_set_tIME: `png_set_tIME` stores a valid PNG `tIME` chunk value in `info_ptr`. Use it before writing; it ignores NULL args, refuses changes after `PNG_WROTE_tIME`, and rejects invalid month/day/time values with a warning.
functions.png_get_image_height: `png_get_image_height` returns the image height in pixels from `info_ptr->height`. Use it with valid `png_ptr` and `info_ptr`; if either is `NULL`, it returns `0`.
functions.png_set_bKGD: `png_set_bKGD` stores a PNG bKGD chunk value in `info_ptr`. Call it with valid `png_ptr`, `info_ptr`, and `background`; it copies the color into `info_ptr->background` and marks `PNG_INFO_bKGD` valid. If any arg is NULL, it does nothing.
functions.png_set_packing: `png_set_packing` requests unpacking 1/2/4-bit samples to 1 byte each. Call it on a valid `png_ptr` before read/write processing. If `bit_depth < 8`, it sets `PNG_PACK` (and write `usr_bit_depth=8`); otherwise it does nothing.
functions.png_set_hIST: `png_set_hIST` stores a PNG palette histogram in `info_ptr`. Use it only after `info_ptr->num_palette` is valid (1..PNG_MAX_PALETTE_LENGTH). If `png_ptr`/`info_ptr` is NULL or palette size is invalid, it returns/warns and does nothing. It frees old hIST data first.
functions.png_set_expand: `png_set_expand` enables automatic expansion transforms. Use it before reading rows to request palette/low-bit/packed/gray+tRNS data be expanded to 8-bit grayscale or 24-bit RGB, with alpha when available. If transforms aren’t allowed, it does nothing.
functions.png_get_uint_16: `png_get_uint_16` reads a 2-byte big-endian value from `buf` and returns it as `png_uint_16`. Use it when parsing PNG data bytes. It simply combines `buf[0]<<8 | buf[1]`; no validation or bounds checking.
functions.png_read_image: `png_read_image` reads the entire image into the caller’s row-pointer array. Use after `png_read_info`/setup, with `image` pointing to enough rows. It handles interlacing if enabled; if not, it warns and may still fix setup. Returns void, no-op if `png_ptr==NULL`.
functions.png_get_rows: `png_get_rows` is a simple accessor for the `row_pointers` array produced by `png_read_png()`. Call it with valid `png_ptr` and `info_ptr`; it returns the scanline pointer array, or `NULL` if either argument is `NULL`.
functions.png_set_check_for_invalid_index: Sets whether libpng should check for invalid palette indices. Call it with `allowed > 0` to disable the check (`num_palette_max=0`); otherwise it enables checking (`-1`). It just sets this internal flag.
functions.png_image_write_to_file: Design: convenience wrapper to write a `png_image` to a named file. Use with valid `image` version, non-NULL `file` and `buffer`; it opens `"wb"` then calls `png_image_write_to_stdio`. Returns 1 on success, 0 on invalid args/open/write/flush/close failure.
functions.png_set_filter: `png_set_filter` selects libpng’s row-filtering for PNG writing. Use `method=0` (`PNG_FILTER_TYPE_BASE`) and a filter mask like `PNG_FILTER_VALUE_NONE/SUB/...`. Invalid filter bits can trigger an error; `png_ptr==NULL` is ignored.
functions.png_set_packswap: `png_set_packswap` enables the `PNG_PACKSWAP` transform for packed images. Call it on a valid `png_ptr`; it only has effect when `bit_depth < 8`. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it does nothing.
functions.png_set_user_limits: Sets per-decoder max image width/height. Call it on a valid `png_structrp` before `png_set_IHDR()`. Images exceeding either limit are rejected; use `0x7fffffff` for “accept any” size. If `png_ptr == NULL`, it does nothing.
functions.png_set_gAMA: `png_set_gAMA` sets the PNG gAMA chunk in `info_ptr` using a double gamma value. It just converts to libpng fixed-point via `png_set_gAMA_fixed`; actual validation/handling is in that helper. Use it when writing image gamma metadata.
functions.png_read_png: `png_read_png()` is a convenience “read whole image” API: it calls `png_read_info()`, applies requested transforms, then reads the image data. Use it only after setting up `png_ptr/info_ptr` and desired transform flags. If `png_ptr`/`info_ptr` is NULL it returns; oversized height triggers `png_error()`.
functions.png_get_int_32: `png_get_int_32` reads a 32-bit signed integer from a PNG byte buffer (big-endian). Use it on PNG data buffers. It returns the signed value, handles negatives via 2’s complement, and returns 0 on invalid/overflow cases for safety.
functions.png_set_gray_to_rgb: `png_set_gray_to_rgb` enables a read transform that expands grayscale images to RGB. Use it before reading rows. It also forces 1/2/4-bit gray to 8-bit first. If read transforms aren’t allowed, it does nothing.
functions.png_set_unknown_chunk_location: Sets the stored location for an unknown chunk in `info_ptr`. Use it only for a valid chunk index after `png_set_unknown_chunks`. If location lacks IHDR/PLTE/AFTER_IDAT, it reports an error and coerces to IHDR or AFTER_IDAT behavior.
functions.png_get_oFFs: `png_get_oFFs` retrieves the image offset metadata (`oFFs` chunk). Call it with valid `png_ptr`, `info_ptr`, and non-NULL output pointers; it fills x/y offsets and unit type, returning `PNG_INFO_oFFs` if present, else 0.
functions.png_get_text: `png_get_text` retrieves text chunks from `info_ptr` and returns their count. Use it with valid `png_ptr`/`info_ptr`; if `text_ptr`/`num_text` are non-NULL, they’re filled in. If no text or args are NULL, it returns 0 and sets `*num_text` to 0 when provided.
functions.png_set_strip_alpha: `png_set_strip_alpha` enables the `PNG_STRIP_ALPHA` transform. Call it on a valid `png_structrp` before reading rows to drop any alpha channel. If read transforms are no longer allowed (`png_rtran_ok` fails), it does nothing.
functions.png_create_read_struct: Creates/initializes a `png_struct` for reading. Pass libpng version, your error context, and error/warn callbacks. If user memory support is off, it uses default allocators; otherwise it delegates to `png_create_read_struct_2`. Returns the read struct or NULL on failure.
functions.png_convert_to_rfc1123: Deprecated helper to format a `png_time` as an RFC1123 date string. Call with a valid `png_structrp` and `ptime`; it writes into `png_ptr->time_buffer` and returns that pointer. If `ptime` is invalid, warns and returns `NULL`; if `png_ptr` is `NULL`, returns `NULL`.
functions.png_get_tIME: `png_get_tIME` retrieves the image’s `tIME` chunk from `info_ptr`. Call it with valid `png_ptr`, `info_ptr`, and non-NULL `mod_time`. If `PNG_INFO_tIME` is set, it stores a pointer to `info_ptr->mod_time` and returns `PNG_INFO_tIME`; otherwise returns 0.
functions.png_set_text_compression_window_bits: Sets the zlib window size for **text chunk compression**. Call it on a valid `png_ptr` before writing text; values are clamped to **8..15** with warnings. `NULL` `png_ptr` is ignored.
functions.png_set_benign_errors: Sets how libpng treats “benign” errors. Call with `allowed!=0` to downgrade `png_benign_error()` to a warning; `0` restores default error handling. It also toggles app warnings/errors to warning mode.
functions.png_set_read_user_chunk_fn: Sets the read-time callback for unknown PNG chunks. Use it to inspect/process or ignore chunks; store your user data in `user_chunk_ptr`. It only assigns the function/pointer, and does nothing if `png_ptr` is NULL.
functions.png_get_current_row_number: Returns the current row being processed, mainly for use inside user transform callbacks. For interlaced images, it’s the row within the current pass/sub-image and resets each pass. If `png_ptr` is NULL, returns `PNG_UINT_32_MAX`.
functions.png_free: `png_free` releases memory allocated by `png_malloc()`. Call it with the same `png_ptr`; if `png_ptr` or `ptr` is `NULL`, it returns immediately. If a user `free_fn` is set, that is used; otherwise it falls back to libpng’s default free.
functions.png_set_sRGB_gAMA_and_cHRM: Sets the image colorspace to sRGB with the given rendering intent. Use it on valid `png_ptr`/`info_ptr`; if sRGB is accepted, libpng also marks gAMA and cHRM for writing, then syncs `info_ptr`. Null args: no-op.
functions.png_get_iCCP: Retrieves the image’s iCCP chunk from `info_ptr`: profile name, uncompressed ICC profile data, and length. Call only after `png_read_info`; returns `PNG_INFO_iCCP` if present, else 0. `compression_type` is always set to `PNG_COMPRESSION_TYPE_BASE` when non-NULL.
functions.png_get_progressive_ptr: Returns the user I/O pointer for progressive (push) read callbacks. Call it with a valid `png_ptr`; it returns `png_ptr->io_ptr`. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it returns `NULL`.
functions.png_convert_from_struct_tm: Converts a `struct tm` into libpng `png_time` fields. Use it to fill an existing `png_time` from a valid `tm`. It only copies/adjusts values (`year=1900+tm_year`, `month=tm_mon+1`); no validation or timezone handling.
functions.png_write_image: `png_write_image` writes an entire image by calling `png_write_row` for each row; if interlacing is enabled, it repeats the rows for each pass. Use it after setting up write info and providing a row-pointer array. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it returns immediately.
functions.png_get_interlace_type: `png_get_interlace_type` returns `info_ptr->interlace_type` for a valid `png_ptr`/`info_ptr`. Use it after reading image info to query the PNG’s interlace mode. If either pointer is `NULL`, it returns `0`.
functions.png_get_tRNS: `png_get_tRNS` retrieves tRNS transparency info from `info_ptr`. Use after reading PNG info; pass non-NULL outputs to receive palette alpha array and/or transparent color. Returns flags if requested data exists, else 0.
functions.png_set_compression_mem_level: Sets zlib’s memory level for compression. Call it before writing/compression starts, with a valid `png_ptr`. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it does nothing; otherwise it just stores `mem_level` in `png_ptr->zlib_mem_level` without validation.
functions.png_get_image_width: Returns the image width from `info_ptr->width`. Use it after `png_read_info`/when `info_ptr` is valid, passing non-NULL `png_ptr` and `info_ptr`. If either is NULL, it returns 0.
functions.png_process_data: `png_process_data` feeds newly available input bytes into libpng’s push/read parser. Call it with valid `png_ptr` and `info_ptr`; if either is `NULL`, it returns. It stores the buffer, then repeatedly processes data until the internal buffer is empty.
functions.png_read_info: `png_read_info` reads the PNG signature and all header/info chunks up to the first image data (`IDAT`). Use it after creating `png_ptr/info_ptr` and before reading pixels. It returns early on NULL args; errors if chunks are out of order (e.g., `IDAT` before `IHDR`).
functions.png_set_sRGB: `png_set_sRGB` marks the image as sRGB and records the rendering intent. Call it only with valid `png_ptr` and `info_ptr`; if either is `NULL`, it returns immediately. It updates `info_ptr->colorspace` via `png_colorspace_set_sRGB` and syncs the info struct.
functions.png_image_begin_read_from_stdio: Begins reading a PNG from a `FILE*` into a `png_image`. Use with a valid `image` (`PNG_IMAGE_VERSION`) and non-NULL `file`; it initializes read state, sets libpng I/O to the stream, then reads the header. Returns 0 on invalid args/init failure, nonzero on success.
functions.png_set_eXIf_1: Stores EXIF data for an eXIf chunk in `info_ptr`. Call with valid `png_ptr/info_ptr`; it frees any existing EXIF, allocates `num_exif` bytes, copies `exif`, and on NULL ptrs returns. If alloc fails, warns and leaves no data.
functions.png_set_chunk_cache_max: `png_set_chunk_cache_max` sets `png_ptr->user_chunk_cache_max`, i.e. the maximum number of chunks libpng will cache. Call it on a valid `png_structrp` before reading. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it does nothing.
functions.png_image_begin_read_from_memory: Design: start a `png_image` read from an in-memory PNG buffer. Use after setting `image->version`; pass non-NULL `memory` and `size>0`. It initializes read state, hooks a memory reader, then reads the PNG header. Invalid args/version return an error.
functions.png_set_read_user_transform_fn: Sets a read-time callback for user-defined pixel transforms. Call it on `png_structrp`; it enables `PNG_USER_TRANSFORM` and stores the function pointer. If read-user-transform support is off, it does nothing.
functions.png_get_copyright: Returns libpng’s copyright/version text as a const string. `png_ptr` is unused and may be NULL. Use it only to display/read the built-in notice; it has no side effects and always returns the compile-time string.
functions.png_write_chunk_end: Ends a chunk begun by `png_write_chunk_start()`: it writes the final 4-byte CRC in one I/O call. Pass a valid `png_ptr`; if `NULL`, it returns immediately. With IO state support, it marks the write as chunk CRC.
functions.png_set_sBIT: `png_set_sBIT` stores the image’s significant-bit info in `info_ptr`. Call it with valid `png_ptr`, `info_ptr`, and `sig_bit`; otherwise it returns immediately. On success it copies `*sig_bit` into `info_ptr->sig_bit` and marks `PNG_INFO_sBIT` valid.
functions.png_set_palette_to_rgb: `png_set_palette_to_rgb` requests libpng to expand paletted images to full RGB, and also expand tRNS transparency if present. Call it before reading image rows. If transformations are already locked out, it does nothing; otherwise it sets `PNG_EXPAND | PNG_EXPAND_tRNS`.
functions.png_reset_zstream: `png_reset_zstream` resets libpng’s zlib inflate stream. Call it with a valid `png_structrp` before reusing decompression state. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it returns `Z_STREAM_ERROR`; otherwise it returns `inflateReset()`’s status.
functions.png_malloc: `png_malloc` allocates `size` bytes using libpng’s memory allocator tied to `png_ptr`. Use it only with a valid `png_ptr`; if `png_ptr==NULL` it returns `NULL`. On allocation failure it calls `png_error(png_ptr, "Out of memory")` instead of returning `NULL`.
functions.png_set_text_compression_strategy: Sets the zlib compression strategy used for PNG text chunks. Call it with a valid `png_structrp` before writing text; `strategy` is stored as-is. If `png_ptr` is `NULL`, it does nothing.
functions.png_set_write_status_fn: Sets the write-row status callback for a PNG write struct. Call it with a valid `png_structrp` before/while writing; passing `NULL` for `png_ptr` does nothing. `write_row_fn` may be `NULL` to clear the callback.
functions.png_set_keep_unknown_chunks:
Sets libpng’s policy for unknown chunks: `keep` chooses default handling; `chunk_list`/`num_chunks` can override per-chunk. `num_chunks<=0` only sets the default. `png_ptr==NULL` returns; invalid `keep` triggers app error.
Yes—this crash is caused by misuse of the API. Pass chunk_list as a sequence of exactly 4-byte PNG chunk names, and ensure num_chunks is the number of 4-byte names present. Do not construct a malformed or truncated buffer, and do not derive num_chunks from data that is not guaranteed to contain complete 4-byte entries. Validate that chunk_list != NULL when num_chunks > 0, that the backing storage contains at least 4*num_chunks bytes, and prefer calling the function once with a well-formed list instead of fuzzing negative or inconsistent counts. In short: provide a valid array of complete 4-byte chunk identifiers and a matching nonnegative count.
functions.png_set_compression_buffer_size: Sets the zlib compression buffer size for a png struct. Call before compression/IDAT use; `size` must be 1..PNG_UINT_31_MAX. On read structs it sets `IDAT_read_size`; on write structs it changes the buffer unless already in use (`zowner!=0`), then warns and leaves it unchanged.
functions.png_get_valid: `png_get_valid` checks whether a given chunk flag is set in `info_ptr->valid`. Use it with non-NULL `png_ptr` and `info_ptr`; it returns the matching valid bits, or 0 if either pointer is NULL or the chunk isn’t marked valid.
functions.png_write_chunk_data: Writes the payload of a chunk begun with `png_write_chunk_start()`, while updating the CRC. Call it with `png_ptr` valid; if `data==NULL` or `length==0`, it does nothing. If `png_ptr==NULL`, it returns immediately.
functions.png_get_io_state: `png_get_io_state()` returns the current I/O state flags stored in `png_ptr->io_state`. Use it on a valid `png_ptr` to inspect libpng’s current read/write progress. It does not modify state; it just reports whatever state is currently set.
functions.png_get_uint_31: `png_get_uint_31` reads a 32-bit big-endian value from `buf` and enforces PNG’s 31-bit unsigned limit. Use it when parsing fields that must fit in `0..PNG_UINT_31_MAX`. If the value is larger, it calls `png_error(png_ptr, "PNG unsigned integer out of range")`; otherwise it returns the value.
functions.png_get_sBIT: `png_get_sBIT` retrieves the image’s stored significant-bit info from `info_ptr`. Call it with valid `png_ptr`, `info_ptr`, and `sig_bit`; on success it sets `*sig_bit` to `info_ptr->sig_bit` and returns `PNG_INFO_sBIT`. Otherwise it returns 0.
functions.png_get_palette_max: Returns the maximum palette size from `png_ptr->num_palette_max`. Use only with non-NULL `png_ptr` and `info_ptr`; otherwise it returns `-1`. It’s a simple query helper, not a setter.
